Safety Protocols & Emergency Codes

Hospital safety protocols and emergency codes — fire, cardiac arrest, infant abduction, violence, evacuation.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • List common emergency codes and their meanings
  • Describe fire safety (RACE, PASS)
  • Explain the nurse's role in emergencies

In simple words

Hospitals use emergency codes to alert staff quickly and standardise responses to emergencies. Nurses must know the codes and their role in each.

Common codes: fire, cardiac arrest, infant abduction, violent person, bomb threat, evacuation, external disaster.

Common emergency codes

Code Meaning Nurse’s action
Code Red Fire Rescue, Alarm, Confine, Extinguish (RACE)
Code Blue Cardiac/respiratory arrest Start CPR; call the resuscitation team
Code Pink Infant/child abduction Secure exits; search; alert security
Code Silver Violent person/weapon Call security; do not confront alone
Code Black Bomb threat Follow evacuation instructions
Code Orange External disaster Prepare for mass casualties
Code Gray Combative person Call security; de-escalate

Fire safety: RACE and PASS

  • RACE: Rescue patients in danger, Activate alarm, Confine fire (close doors), Extinguish or Evacuate.
  • PASS: Pull pin, Aim at base of fire, Squeeze handle, Sweep side to side.

🔴 Fire: RACE and PASS

RACE: Rescue, Alarm, Confine, Extinguish. PASS: Pull pin, Aim at base, Squeeze handle, Sweep side to side.

Where the nurse uses this

  • Know the codes — memorise your hospital’s code meanings and response.
  • Code Blue — start CPR if trained; call the resuscitation team; bring the crash cart.
  • Fire — use RACE and PASS; know nearest extinguisher and exit.
  • Code Pink — secure exits; do not let anyone leave with a baby; alert security.
  • Violent person — call security; keep distance; do not confront alone.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Emergency codes alert staff quickly to different emergencies.
  2. Code Red = fire; Code Blue = cardiac/respiratory arrest; Code Pink = infant/child abduction.
  3. Code Silver = violent person/weapon; Code Black = bomb threat; Code Orange = external disaster.
  4. Fire: RACE (Rescue, Alarm, Confine, Extinguish); PASS (Pull, Aim, Squeeze, Sweep).
  5. Code Blue: start CPR if trained; call the resuscitation team.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Know your hospital’s specific codes — they can vary.
  2. Code Pink: secure exits; prevent abduction; alert security.
  3. Code Silver/Black: call security; follow evacuation instructions.
  4. RACE: Rescue patients first, then alarm, confine, extinguish/evacuate.
  5. PASS: aim at the base of the fire, not the flames.

📌 Memory trick

RACE: “Rescue, Alarm, Confine, Extinguish.” PASS: “Pull, Aim, Squeeze, Sweep.”

60-second revision

  • Emergency codes = standardised alerts for emergencies.
  • Code Red = fire; Code Blue = arrest; Code Pink = infant abduction; Code Silver = violent person.
  • Fire: RACE (Rescue, Alarm, Confine, Extinguish); PASS (Pull, Aim, Squeeze, Sweep).
  • Code Blue: CPR + call resuscitation team.
  • Know your hospital’s codes.

Test yourself

Code Blue means:

Answer: B. Code Blue is cardiac or respiratory arrest — start CPR and call the resuscitation team.

Code Pink means:

Answer: B. Code Pink is infant or child abduction — secure exits and alert security.

In RACE fire safety, R stands for:

Answer: B. RACE: Rescue, Alarm, Confine, Extinguish — rescue patients in danger first.

In PASS extinguisher use, A stands for:

Answer: B. PASS: Pull pin, Aim at base of fire, Squeeze handle, Sweep side to side.

Code Silver is:

Answer: B. Code Silver is a violent person or weapon situation — call security.
